title: Asana Review (2026)
intro: Asana is evaluated here as a work OS / work management platform — Asana is a work management platform for tasks, projects, portfolios and goals with strong adoption for marketing, ops and cross-functional teams. Free covers limited users; Starter is $10.99/user/mo annual; Advanced $24.99; Enterprise custom. AI Studio / AI Teammates packaging rides paid tiers with credit models — confirm live. Distinct from engineering trackers like Jira. This review uses SoftwareGlimpse’s project-management methodology (ease of use, work planning, automation, collaboration, integrations, reporting, scalability, value, AI), scoring products inside their job cluster rather than against unrelated peers. It is based on first-party research, not hands-on lab testing.
summary: Choose Asana when cross-functional teams need clear ownership, goals and workflows without an engineering-tracker learning curve.
verdict: Choose Asana when cross-functional teams need clear ownership, goals and workflows without an engineering-tracker learning curve. Compare monday.com/ClickUp for Work OS configurability, Hive for lower SMB floors, and Jira/Linear if the buyer job is software delivery. Scores reflect first-party documentation as of 2026-08-17 — not hands-on product testing. Confirm current packaging, minimums and usage rates on the vendor site before purchase.

criterionAssessments.rationale: Asana is repeatedly positioned for fast adoption by non-technical cross-functional teams — high ease vs engineering trackers.
Tasks, projects, timelines, portfolios and goals give a strong Work OS planning envelope peer to monday.com.
Rules and workflow builders are strong on Advanced+; Starter is lighter — held at 8 vs monday’s 9.
Comments, proofing-adjacent workflows and cross-team ownership are core strengths.
Broad native + Zapier ecosystem; slightly behind monday’s published breadth narrative.
Dashboards and goals reporting solid on Advanced; not a BI suite.
Clear Free → Starter → Advanced → Enterprise path for mid-market and up.
Starter $10.99 sits above ClickUp/monday Basic floors; capability justifies mid-market spend. Affiliate economics excluded.
AI Studio / Teammates marketed on paid tiers with credit packaging — strong capability with TCO friction.

bestFor: Buyers prioritising adoption ease and goals/workflows
notIdealFor: Engineering sprint orgs that need Jira/Linear
Teams wanting the cheapest all-in-one seat (ClickUp)
cons: Can feel light vs monday for ops configurability
limitations: Advanced features and deeper automation often require Advanced+
AI Studio credit packaging can raise TCO beyond Starter seat floors
Not optimised as an engineering sprint tracker
Free plan is limited versus ClickUp’s unlimited-user Free narrative
pricingSummary: Free limited; Starter $10.99, Advanced $24.99 per user/mo annual; Enterprise custom. AI on paid tiers. Confirm live.
whoShouldChoose: Choose Asana when cross-functional teams need clear ownership, goals and workflows without an engineering-tracker learning curve.
whoShouldConsiderAlternatives: Compare monday.com/ClickUp for Work OS configurability, Hive for lower SMB floors, and Jira/Linear if the buyer job is software delivery.

faq.question: Is Asana a project management / work OS tool?
faq.answer: Yes. Asana is evaluated as a work OS / work management platform for boards, timelines, automations and team collaboration on work. It is not monday sales CRM — that remains a separate CRM product entity where applicable.

faq.question: How is Asana priced?
faq.answer: Free limited; Starter $10.99, Advanced $24.99 per user/mo annual; Enterprise custom. AI on paid tiers. Confirm live.

faq.question: Does Asana have a free plan or free trial?
faq.answer: Yes — a free plan is published. A free trial is documented. Confirm current terms with the vendor.

faq.question: Did SoftwareGlimpse personally test Asana?
faq.answer: No. This review is based on first-party product and pricing research evidence, not hands-on product usage. Affiliate relationships never influence scores.
